Inflation fears intensified in September, pushing the near-term outlook in the New York Federal Reserve's monthly survey to its highest level in nearly 3½ years.

The central bank's Survey of Consumer Expectations indicated that the median view for inflation over the next 12 months rose to 3.9%, up 0.3 percentage point from August and the highest level since May 2023, when the figure was at 4.1%. [...] Similarly, the survey found that household spending growth is expected to hit 5.5%, also up 0.3 percentage point month over month and the highest since May 2023.

results.content: The final inflation report voters will see before the 2026 midterms showed prices rose at an even faster pace than expected in September, another blow for President Donald Trump and Republicans as they confront significant headwinds in an election heavily focused on affordability. Core inflation—which strips out the more volatile food and energy categories—came in at 0.3 percent and 2.6 percent on a monthly and annual basis, respectively. results.content: WASHINGTON (AP) — American confidence in the economy rebounded somewhat in October as gas prices fell modestly, though it remains much more expensive to fill up a tank than last year at this time. The Conference Board said Tuesday that its consumer confidence index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October from 84.2 last month. According to the auto club AAA, the average price for a gallon of regular gas in the U.S. was $4.27 Tuesday, down from $4.48 a month ago. Last year at this time, a gallon of regular in the U.S. averaged $3.05.
